title: PV Loops and REBOA During Hemorrhage and Resuscitation
protocol: Anesthetize the animal with telazol and xylazine at appropriate doses.
Transport the animal to the procedure area.
Place the animal under isoflurane targeting 1.0 MAC by facemask.
Transition to generally 10 ccs/kg TV, RR of 12-14 initially but adjust as needed to target a pCO2 of 30-45 and an FiO2 of 40%.
Place the animal in sternal recumbency and intubate with a 7.0 endotracheal tube.
Make the animal supine and restrain.
Place all venous and arterial catheters using US guidance, and place all monitoring devices.
Place an LV PV loop via a carotid or right brachial artery 7 fr sheath catheter.
Place a 7 fr sheath in either jugular down to the RA to obtain central venous gases (and labs).
Place a 7 fr sheath in one carotid artery.
Through the sheath placed in the carotid artery, place an aortic pressure probe proximal to the REBOA site.
Place a 7 fr sheath in either jugular vein for central venous pressure measurement.
Insert an at least 7 fr sheath into either femoral vein for hemorrhaging and resuscitation purposes.
Place a 7 fr sheath in one femoral artery, through which place another aortic pressure probe distal to the REBOA site.
Place an at least 8 fr (preferably 9 fr) sheath in one femoral artery to secure the REBOA catheter from below.
Attach EKG leads, oxygen saturation monitor, rectal temperature sensor, and a grounding pad after shaving the necessary area.
Perform a lower abdominal laparotomy for cystostomy, placing a Foley catheter into the bladder.
Perform a left anterolateral thoracotomy to place a 3 or 4 mm flow probe around the coronary artery. Apply ultrasound jelly to the flow probe.
Confirm all line placements.
Confirm that all sheaths work by performing a drawback and flush.
Ensure fluids are ready for administration.
Reset the timer to ensure it is functioning correctly.
Verify that data is being transduced through LabChart via appropriately labeled channels and saved.
Check ventilatory settings.
Confirm fluoroscopically that all catheters and devices are positioned appropriately.
Give 1L of 0.9% NS at the start.
Administer one 50cc D50 at the beginning.
Obtain VBG, ABG, Trop, Chem8, and collect five tubes of serum.
Treat with one ampule of Calcium at the start of resuscitation if glucose levels are below 65 mg/dL.
For a pH less than 7.2, administer one ampule of bicarbonate.
Manage pCO2 as necessary by adjusting mechanical ventilation settings.
During resuscitation, treat sustained MAP less than 65 mmHg after starting fluids with norepinephrine as the first-line pressor.
Enter baseline blood resistivity into the PV catheter system control.
Bleed at a rate of 50ccs per minute from venous CVC to achieve a goal systolic BP of 45 mmHg.
Maintain SPB between 45-50 mmHg during shock phase and bleed further if necessary.
Obtain VBG at the end of shock period.
Collect ABG if pO2 was low or clinically indicated before.
Obtain repeat blood resistivity.
If needed, enter new value into PV catheter system.
End Full REBOA period with VBG and ABG.
Start Partial REBOA period.
Aim for 50% SPB differential between above and below REBOA aortic pressure transducers.
Allow stabilization for 15 minutes.
Begin fluid resuscitation.
Return all shed blood and one ampule of Calcium.
Give up to 3L of 0.9% NS as needed.
End Partial REBOA period with Full Deflation.
Transition to post REBOA ICU period.
Obtain VBG and ABG at the start of ICU period.
Confirm ventilatory stability.
Euthanize and dispose of animal.
Clean equipment.
